description: Use this when the user asks which drugs or therapies are in development against a target, a mechanism, a hallmark of aging or an age-related disease, who develops them and how far each has got. Lists drug and therapy programmes (assets), furthest stage first: each with its developers and partners, code names, modality, targets, mechanism, indications with the stage of each, hallmarks of aging and lifespan evidence. Narrow by target (a gene symbol such as GLP1R, or a process), mechanism words, modality, hallmark, indication, stage, the developer's country, an organisation or a name. Read one in full with get_asset; count them with count_pipeline. An account whose plan includes drug and therapy programmes reads every record in full; others read an outline, as the site's asset pages show it.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from `pagination.next_cursor` of the previous page. Keep the other parameters the same.

hallmark.description: A hallmark of aging the asset acts on.

indication.description: A disease, by name or entity key (`idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis`, `alzheimer-disease`).

mechanism.description: Words that must all appear in the asset's mechanism line (case-insensitive).

organisation.description: An organisation key: the assets it develops, partners on or licensed out.

q.description: Letters and digits in any of the asset's names or code names (`UBX1325` matches UBX-1325).

stage.description: Stage: with `indication`, the stage for that indication; otherwise the asset's furthest stage.

target.description: A target: a gene symbol or key (`GLP1R`, `bcl2l1`) or a process key (`mtor`, `cellular-senescence`).

name: list_assets
